note: How the predictor page adapts this repository's build. The page's generator (richardparslow-commits/life-policy-light, scripts/embed-estimator.mjs) reads this file and applies these four adaptations, copying everything else byte for byte, and check-consumer-parity.js applies the same file to the same build — one description of the page, read by the script that writes it and the check that judges it, instead of two copies that can drift. `inserts` adds lines at a build anchor, `omits` drops the build statement that starts at an anchor, `rewrites` replaces a fixed number of occurrences. The check applies them to the build and requires the page's document to begin with the result, followed by the page's own render-time adapters, so the page is held to this build exactly. A missing build anchor, a page that still carries an omitted statement, and a document that is not that composition all fail: the first two mean the page cannot be regenerated from this build or no longer matches its own description, the last means it is not this build. `releaseClaims` describes the other thing the page states about the build: which release it runs. Each claim is literal text with `{version}` where the number goes, matched against the build's own HCE_VERSION in every place it is declared — the committed page's source and the served page — so a page serving the right bytes cannot tell a reader or a crawler that it is an older release. The page's generator stamps the same claims, which is why the two cannot drift apart: softwareVersion sat at 78 while the page ran 80 only because it was hand-typed and nothing compared it.
